youtube.aciklama:
An audiometer is a device that produces calibrated test sounds and delivers them through earphones, a bone vibrator or a loudspeaker. In this lesson we compare the frequency, intensity, presentation and output controls, zero dB HL and calibration, continuous and pulsed tones, supra-aural and insert earphones, the bone vibrator and the sound-field loudspeaker.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology; Gelfand, Essentials of Audiology; IEC 60645-1, Electroacoustics - Audiometric equipment - Part 1: Equipment for pure-tone and speech audiometry; ANSI S3.6, Specification for Audiometers; ISO 389 series, Acoustics - Reference zero for the calibration of audiometric equipment.

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will get to know the audiometer, the basic tool of pure-tone audiometry, and its controls.
We will compare the transducers that deliver sound to the ear: earphones, the bone vibrator and the loudspeaker.

cumleler.yazi: An audiometer is an electronic device that produces calibrated test sounds at set frequencies and intensities.

cumleler: The sounds it produces are delivered to the ear or the skull through transducers.
Earphones are used for air-conduction testing, and a bone vibrator for bone-conduction testing.
When the patient hears the sound, they press the response button and a light comes on at the device.
The features and accuracy of audiometers are defined by international standards.
Standards divide audiometers into types, from full clinical devices to screening devices that test air conduction only.

ogeler.metin: Turns the sound on and off

cumleler: Every audiometer has a few basic controls.
The frequency control selects the tone frequency; air conduction usually covers one hundred twenty five to eight thousand hertz.
The intensity control, or attenuator, changes the level in decibels HL, in five decibel steps on most devices.
The tone presenter delivers the sound at the chosen moment and for the chosen duration.
The output selector sends the sound to the right or left earphone, the bone vibrator or the loudspeaker.
On two-channel devices, the second channel is used to deliver masking noise to the non-test ear.
An audiometer's zero decibels HL is not silence; it is the average threshold of young people with normal hearing.
This zero point matches a different sound pressure level for each frequency and each transducer; these values are given in standards.
That is why normal hearing appears on the audiogram as a flat line around zero at all frequencies.
A brief daily listening check of the device is recommended.
In addition, the audiometer is usually calibrated with measuring equipment at least once a year.
Thresholds found with a poorly calibrated device are wrong, however correct the method.
Clinical audiometers also have a microphone input and an input for recorded material for speech tests.

cumleler.yazi: The speech level is monitored and adjusted with a meter called the VU meter.
cumleler.ses: The speech level is monitored and adjusted with a meter called the V.U. meter.

cumleler: For masking there are options such as narrowband noise, speech noise and broadband noise.
There is also a talkback system for two-way conversation between the booth and the control room.
We will use these sections in detail in the speech audiometry and masking lessons.

ogeler.metin: Unbroken while the key is held
Pulsed tones are easier to notice
Helps tell it from the ringing

cumleler: The test tone can be given as continuous or pulsed; both are used in the clinic.
A continuous tone plays without a break as long as the tone key is held down.
In a pulsed tone, the sound switches on and off several times a second.
Pulsed tones make the sound easier to notice for many patients.
Especially in patients with tinnitus, a pulsed tone helps tell the test sound apart from the ringing.
In tests through a loudspeaker, frequency-modulated tones, whose frequency wobbles slightly, are used.
The tone always switches on and off smoothly so no click is heard; what matters is using a consistent mode for the same patient.
A supra-aural earphone is a cushioned earphone that sits on top of the pinna.

cumleler.yazi: Models used in the clinic for many years include the TDH-39 and the DD45.
cumleler.ses: Models used in the clinic for many years include the T.D.H. thirty nine and the D.D. forty five.

cumleler: It is quick and easy to put on; nothing goes into the ear canal, so it is comfortable for people with sensitive ear canals.
Its interaural attenuation is low, about forty decibels, so masking is needed more often.
In some people, the pressure of the earphone can cause the ear canal to collapse, a collapsing ear canal.
The ear cushion reduces room noise only to a limited extent.

etiketler.metin: Foam tip in the ear canal

cumleler: An insert earphone delivers sound into the ear canal through a thin tube and a foam tip.

cumleler.yazi: Common models in the clinic include the ER-3A and the IP30.
cumleler.ses: Common models in the clinic include the E.R. three A and the I.P. thirty.

cumleler: Its interaural attenuation is higher; the conservative value is about fifty five decibels, and it is even higher at low frequencies.
Because it keeps the ear canal open, it prevents collapse and isolates room noise better.
The foam tips are single-use, which is also an advantage for hygiene.
However, it may not be usable if there is discharge in the ear canal or the canal has not developed, that is, atresia.
Both earphone types have a place in the clinic; the choice depends on the patient and the test.
A supra-aural earphone is quick to fit, and nothing has to go into the ear canal.
On the other hand, its interaural attenuation is low and it carries a risk of canal collapse.
An insert earphone reduces the need for masking, prevents collapse and isolates room noise better.
But the right tip size must be chosen and the tip inserted to an adequate depth.
Supra-aural earphones have long been widely used, and the use of insert earphones keeps growing.
The earphone type determines how easily the test sound crosses to the other ear.
With a supra-aural earphone, a seventy decibel sound, attenuated by forty decibels, can reach the other cochlea at about thirty decibels.
With an insert earphone, the same sound is attenuated by at least fifty five decibels and reaches the other side at about fifteen decibels.
So with insert earphones, fewer frequencies need masking, especially in asymmetric losses.
We will cover the rules of masking in detail in separate lessons later.

cumleler.yazi: A bone vibrator turns the electrical signal into mechanical vibration that is carried to the skull.
Common models in the clinic include the B-71 and the B-81.
cumleler.ses: Common models in the clinic include the B seventy one and the B eighty one.

cumleler: The vibrator is placed on the mastoid or the forehead with a headband.
Its maximum output is much lower than that of earphones, and the test range is usually two hundred fifty to four thousand hertz.
In bone conduction, interaural attenuation is about zero, so unmasked bone conduction reflects the better of the two cochleae.
In sound-field testing, sound is given from a loudspeaker in the booth instead of through earphones.
The patient sits at a set distance and angle from the loudspeaker, and calibration is done for this listening position.
To avoid standing waves in the room, frequency-modulated tones or narrowband noise are used instead of pure tones.
Because the sound reaches both ears, the result reflects the hearing of the better ear.
Sound field is used with young children who will not wear earphones, and for measurements with hearing aids or implants.
If the patient's head position changes, the sound level reaching the ear changes too, so the seating position is kept fixed.

sahneler.metin: Before the day starts, give every earphone and the vibrator a brief listening check. Cable crackle, swapped right and left, or lost sound can silently ruin results.
cumleler: A clinical tip: every morning, before the first patient, do a brief listening check of the audiometer.
Listen to a few frequencies at a low level through each earphone and the vibrator, and confirm right and left come from the correct side.
Gently move the cables to check for crackling or dropouts.
This short check protects the reliability of every measurement made during the day.
The basic controls of an audiometer are frequency, intensity, tone presentation and output selection.
Zero decibels HL is the average threshold of young people with normal hearing and is calibrated separately for each transducer.
Insert earphones give higher interaural attenuation than supra-aural earphones and prevent canal collapse.
With the bone vibrator, interaural attenuation is about zero, and a sound-field result reflects the better-hearing ear.

sahneler.soru: Which transducer has the highest interaural attenuation?
sahneler.aciklama: Conservative IA is about _55 dB_ for inserts, 40 dB for supra-aural, 0 dB for the vibrator.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: which transducer has the highest interaural attenuation?
The correct answer is B: the insert earphone.

cumleler: The conservative value is about fifty five decibels for insert earphones, forty for supra-aural earphones and zero for the bone vibrator.
